uncited: This method aggregates pixel-aligned features from an arbitrary number of input views into a single feature vector for a query 3D point, solving the problem of variable input dimensions at inference time.

It differs from simple mean pooling by injecting camera parameters into the aggregation process to mitigate artifacts caused by depth ambiguity, and it differs from fixed-view concatenation by being permutation invariant to the number of conditioning views.

**Projection and Sampling:** For each conditioning view $i$, project the 3D point $X$ onto the 2D feature image plane using the camera intrinsic $K$ and extrinsic parameters $R, t$ to obtain 2D coordinates.
This variant explicitly injects viewpoint information into the feature aggregation.
It uses a network $N_{cf}$ to transform features conditioned on camera parameters (quaternion and position) before averaging.
- **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of conditioning views $n$, as it requires one forward pass through $N_{cf}$ per view and one summation.
- **Memory Complexity:** Linear with respect to $n$ to store intermediate features before aggregation.
- **Strengths:** Handles arbitrary numbers of input views at inference; reduces artifacts caused by depth ambiguity by leveraging camera geometry.
- **Limitations:** Requires training a separate network $N_{cf}$; performance depends on the accuracy of the camera parameter encoding.

The work addresses the limitation of previous methods that required a fixed number of conditioning views or suffered from artifacts when using simple mean pooling in multi-view settings with depth ambiguity.

Originated in the PVA (Pixel-aligned Volumetric Avatars) paper [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method originated in the PVA paper [S1]. However, the provided text from Source [S1] explicitly states: 'A simple permutation invariant function for feature aggregation is the mean of the sampled features (as employed in PIFu [22]).' This indicates that the basic mean aggregation technique was employed in PIFu, not originated in PVA. While PVA introduces camera-aware aggregation to improve upon this, the claim that the entire concept/method originated in PVA is contradicted by the text attributing the foundational aggregation method to PIFu.

The claim states that the method must handle $n$ varying at inference time and that simple concatenation is insufficient because it requires a fixed number of views. Source [S1] explicitly states in Section 3.3.2: 'The more interesting use case is to make the model agnostic to viewpoint and number of conditioning views. Simple concatenation as above is insufficient in this case, since we do not know the number of conditioning views a priori, leading to different feature dimensions during inference time.' This directly supports both parts of the claim.

Sample the feature vector $f_X^{(i)}$ from the feature map $f^{(i)}$ at these coordinates [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the feature vector $f_X^{(i)}$ is sampled from the feature map $f^{(i)}$ at specific coordinates. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly describes this process in Section 3.2 and Section 4. Specifically, it states: 'For each (i) feature map f (i) , we obtain fX ∈ d by projecting 3D point X along the ray using camera intrinsic and extrinsic parameters K, R, t of that particular viewpoint'. This confirms that the sampling occurs at coordinates derived from projecting the 3D point X via the camera parameters, which matches the 'coordinates [S1, unofficial]' description in the claim.
